utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminary matters were announced. The Chamber received, it was filed yesterday, a waiver of attendance signed by Mr. Mladic. He waives his right to attend trial today, and he announces that he'll be back on the 16th of March, which is next Monday. Could we verify whether the videolink through which we'll hear the testimony of the next witness is functioning well. Madam Registrar can you hear me, can you see me?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours. I hereby confirm that we can see and we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you inform us who is present in the videolink room.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honour, apart from myself, there is an ICTY technical officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we are, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- no protective measures, Mr. Rodic being your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you escort Mr. Rodic into the videolink room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Rodic. Mr. Rodic, can you see us? Can you hear us? I ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, before you give evidence the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you by Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Lukic. You'll soon see him on your screen. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rodic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you provide a written statement to the members of the Mladic Defence team, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please state your name for the record but do it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Miso Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before we start, I would like to inform the Trial Chamber about some corrections in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, in paragraph 2, in English version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you give the document number please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please, can we have 1D1713 on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it wouldn't surprise me if you would correct the 35th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any better number for that in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do. It's 31st of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 31st of May. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And paragraphs 30 and 31 reference -- we have reference to three documents -- actually, two different documents, but none of these references should be included in those paragraphs. So one of the documents is mentioned in paragraph 6 and it should be there but not in paragraphs 30 and 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is that? What document is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 18387.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In both paragraphs 30 and 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And also paragraph 65 ter 1D02907.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly switch off unnecessary microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 1 on our screens, please, of -- from the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rodic, on the screen before you, you can see the first page of the document. Do you see the signature? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it; do you know?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we go to the last page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see the signature and do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Again, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, did you have an occasion to review your statement? Has everything been recorded just as you stated before the Mladic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is contained in the statement, is it truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, would your answers be the same, in principle?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The content of my answers would be the same. The wording may differ, but the content would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we would like to tender Mr. Rodic's statement into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand it's being tendered confidentially and we have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, reference is made to a person. It needs to be confidential. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D1713 receives number D930.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D930 is admitted, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read the statement summary for Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please -- and please keep in mind, Mr. Lukic, that it's especially because of paragraph 31 that the document is admitted under seal. Please keep that in mind also when reading your summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your microphone is on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will first read statement summary of Mr. Rodic with your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Miso Rodic took part in the war since 21st November, 1992, when he was mobilised as a reserve member of the JNA. First he went to the war theatre in Croatia. In February 1992, the brigade command sent him to the 1st Krajina Corps commission for the preparation of the rules regarding the rights of fighters. He performed this duty until 31st of May, 1991 -- 1992. After his return to Prijedor to his brigade, he served in the morale, religious, legal, and political affairs organ. In early May 1992, he was temporarily resettled to the intelligence and security organ, and this can be considered the beginning of his engagement in the intelligence organ. Mr. Rodic will testify about his knowledge regarding military organisation of Muslims and Croats in the area of Prijedor. Mr. Rodic was not present in Prijedor on 30th of May, 1992, when the attack on Prijedor took place. But immediately after the first members of the Green Berets taking part in the attack on Prijedor were captured, he took part in their interrogation and found out about their objectives and intentions concerning the manner of taking over power in Prijedor. During the questioning of the 2nd lieutenant Asim Muhic, he found out that Mr. Muhic had taken part in the training of Green Berets members while being a member of the 6th Sana Infantry Brigade of the JNA, which held positions in Jasenovac. Mr. Rodic interrogated Mr. Cirkin, professional soldier, who was deputy to the military commander in Kozarac, as well as other members of Green Berets. During the interrogation Sead Cirkin categorically stated that neither the Crisis Staff of Kozarac nor the Green Berets command had been in favour of any peaceful solution, and they were certain that they would win the armed conflict. He stressed that he would have been successful in that endeavour if he had been given the necessary weapons. According to the information available to Mr. Rodic, the 43rd Motorised Brigade postponed the use of force, thus creating the opportunity for the Crisis Staff of the Muslim people in the territory of Prijedor municipality to accept the existing situation; i.e., Republika Srpska and the VRS. In that case, all the ethnicities in the territory of Prijedor municipality would be guaranteed safety. Mr. Rodic will testify about his knowledge about collection centres in the area of Prijedor and about the incidents alleged in the indictment. And that concludes statement summary -- summary statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any further questions, Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. Thank you. First, we would call -- and I spoke with my colleague this morning, Mr. Traldi, that we should go through the list of members of group Slavko Ecimovic lead, so we need 1D2907 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rodic, this document is attached to your statement. Did you get involved in the drafting of the list of those people who had participated in the attack on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many people could you identify as attackers on Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: As far as the number of Green Berets soldiers are concerned, there were about 150 of them, according to Muhic's statement. We started collecting intelligence to be able to name those 150. We arrived at total of 112 names of the people for whom there was strong evidence that they had participated in the attack on Prijedor. There were four other names but their identification was not final. In other words, 116 people have been identified based on several sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise any of the names on the first page? Did you interrogate any of these people?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I recognise the name of Slavko Ecimovic; Nedzad Babic, who was my neighbour; Kemal Alagic, also known as Divljak, I interrogated him in late 1995 towards the end of the war. And as for the others I don't think --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you interrogate Slavko Ecimovic also?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this document at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're tendering the document but you were speaking when the previous translation was still ongoing. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D2907 receives number D931.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D931 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you something else. We saw what you did in the course of the war. And what do you do today?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I am the chief of the Department for the Protection of Veterans in the city administration of the town of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's repetitious, Mr. Lukic, because that's written in paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, you're right. And now I would like to call up document D767.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a cover letter which accompanied a number of documents that I'm going to show you. I'm going to ask you about what you see at the bottom of the page, where it says department Chief Miso Rodic. Is this your signature?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Not mine. It is a signature of an authorised official in my department who is authorised to sign documents like this, and I know that this document was indeed dispatched from my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Nenad Babic. He is a desk officer in my department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we go to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is a list of servicemen and the book, log-book number is 1A to K. Can you please tell us what is VOB-8 record?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: What we see is a copy of the VOB-8 original that I keep in my department for the 43rd Motorised Brigade. It is a record maintained by a unit about the members of that unit. There are lists after this page in printed version, and these records are maintained manually by entering the names into already prescribed forms. This shows when a soldier joined the unit, when he left the unit, and also provides data about every soldier's military specialty, i.e., whether is he an infantryman or an artillery man, and so on and so forth. The record is kept for as long as the unit exists, whether in peacetime or in wartime, when it is deployed in action or whether it is engaged in manoeuvres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am making a short pause after your answer to give the interpreters the chance to interpret your words properly.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: That's not a problem. If necessary, I can slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe if we had the B/C/S list only and then we can enlarge it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rodic, now I would like you to look at the document in front of you. I need your explanation about a line -- or rather, an explanation of all the entries in that line from left to right. Just take any name and tell us about that person.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The first person is Ljubomir Aramanda. I don't know whether I'm reading this well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: This is a printed version. In the original, this is a form. So the first is the number, this number 243. The second column contains the first name, the last name, and the father's name. So this is an entry for Ljubomir Aramanda whose father's name was Sreten. After that, the column depicts date of birth and where he was born. The next column is about the municipality from which he was sent to serve in the army and the persons's identity number. The following column depicts the person's rank and his military specialty. In this case, 11301 denotes a certain specialty. I don't know what it is; in other words, it says whether that person is an infantryman or artillery man or a communications man or any other branch of the military and what knowledges he acquired during his compulsory military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the next column, the date of joining?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, no. The next column is the war unit. 8090 is the number of the war unit that the person joins.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next column?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: After that is the date of joining. That's the date when the person came and joined the unit. And the next column depicts the day when the person left. We can see that the date of joining and the date of leaving is entered twice. We can notice that. That means that in the VOB-8 after entering a certain name, if the soldier leaves the unit, he has to be accounted for. The reason why he left was wilful abandonment of the unit. Most common reason for leaving a unit is demobilisation or reassignment to a different unit. Or, alternatively, such a person has been assigned to war work obligation. There are other reasons such as wounding, permanent disability, or death. That is also the reason to enter the person as having left the unit. If the -- such a person returns to the unit again, he is again entered as somebody who joined the unit. This person, Ljubomir Aramanda, returned on 26th of June, 1999, and stayed in the unit until 1993 and deserted the unit again. And the next column is the basis or the grounds for striking the person off the list. If somebody was demobilised, that has to be based on a document, and the document bears a number. That number is entered in this column. It can be reassignment, work obligation, and so on and so forth. And the last column is the date when that person was finally stricken off the list of soldiers in that unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document we have before us, is it the total register according to VOB-8?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: What you received is not a full record. It consists of two large volumes containing data on all military conscripts that went through the 43rd unit. There may have been over 10.000 names entered. This is just a sample, but the principle that was applied was the same for everyone in the register.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have a full register in your archives?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, it exists, and the original is with the corresponding ministry of the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could your organ enter changes in this register?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, only the relevant ministry could.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which one is it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of Labour and Veterans Protection and Social Welfare with the government of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was your job concerning this register?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: In February 2005, we took over military records from the previous Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska that ceased to exist. We took over all of their military records. If a party needs some certificate that stems from this register in order to exercise their rights, we issue such certificates. We also keep the records up to date. If there is a decision made by the relevant ministry in terms of any changes for the register, we carry out those changes. On the topic of VOB-8, when a unit ceases to exist, VOB-8 is terminated, and all the data contained therein is carried over to the individual files of each conscript where all the other data, more comprehensive data is contained beyond what is contained in the VOB-8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could I seek clarification on your issue. Witness, you were asked whether you could change the data. You said no, you couldn't, only the competent ministry could do. Later you say that if they decided that a change should be made that you would implement that change. Does that mean that physically you could but you are not allowed to do it? Because how could you make the changes -- how could you implement the changes that were decided if you can't change anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The individual files for each and every conscript are kept by the relevant departments in town and city administrations. They keep them as records from which they could see data needed for certificates to be issued to the individual citizens to exercise their rights. The ministry I cited is the only body authorised to and make any changes. When they issue a decision on amendment or change of data, for example, with Ljubomir Aramanda, when they say that it wasn't the 26th of June, 1992, but rather the 26th of May, 1992, on the basis of their decision we enter the changes in his individual file and we also note down that it was done pursuant to the ministry decision. Without that decision, we are not allowed to enter changes. Of course, someone could physically make or enter changes unlawfully. But if it did happen, I think it happened seldom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it looks very much as if this is a computerised system. Did you have an electronic version of this list or did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, this is a re-typed VOB of the 43rd Motorised Brigade and we kept a copy. The original, the one in handwriting, is with the ministry. The list we see on the screen contains the data from the template forms that were filled in the relevant units, and they came in a number of different sheets stapled together or in the shape of a log-book containing such template forms. As far as I know, this printed form that we have now was created in late 1995 or early 1996. There are two additional copies to this. A similar printed copy is preserved by the ministry as well as the handwritten one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm still -- I'm still not certain that I understand you. Do you -- are you telling us that this is a typewritten version, or is it a printout of a computerised system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now whether it was printed by a computer or another machine is something I don't know. I don't know how it was done. As far as I can see, I think it was produced by a piece of equipment, but I don't know any other technicalities. I wasn't present in the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you only had a paper copy and nothing else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We, in our department, have only this copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, did the BiH prosecution inquire about these excerpts or registers with you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. We used this database to provide information to the interested party and to official bodies. It is common practice that the prosecutor's office of BiH asked for information about certain individuals. We always provide such information. In order to protect personal information, a third party may not be issued with such information. It has to be requested by a competent organ or by me. That is how you came into possession of the -- this information, because you, as the Defence team, asked for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would now tender this document into evidence. It has its number, D767. It was not admitted. That's why we have to readmit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll have a few questions about this document as well on cross-examination, and I wonder if I might reserve my position until then, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll postpone our decision on admission. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I at this point in time put a question to the witnesses about a certain name he mentioned. Mr. Rodic, you said that the document we saw a minute ago was signed on your behalf by a person with the name Nenad Babic. Earlier, you referred to a similar name in the list of people in Green Berets. Then you said, page 8, line 21: "I recognise the name of Slavko Ecimovic; Nedzad Babic," it's not correctly written here, Barbic, "who was my neighbour..." Is that the same person or are these two different persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are different people. And you misheard the name. The first name is Nenad whereas the other one was Nedzad. Nedzad is a Muslim name, whereas Nenad is a Serbian or Croatian name. Babic is a kind of last name that could be either of the three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] We want to see the next document, please, D768.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 16, line 25, "any of the three."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see the same cover letter again. We are interested in the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is a personal file. Please tell us what it is briefly. Who is it kept for?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: In addition to the VOB-8 where we have summary data, there are also military records kept individually for each and every military conscript. We see here the personal file of Stipo Tomic. These kind of files were kept for officers, commissioned officers, only. Non-commissioned officers did not have such personal files. In other words, this was an officer who completed his education for reserve officer in 1969. There's also other kind of personal information and his promotion to the rank that was held last. We have around 720 such personal files, more or less. It means that there were 720 people who completed their education in the schools for reserve officers and whose rank was higher than second lieutenant; that is to say, from second lieutenant and upwards. They had their personal files. Such officers who were NCOs, the rank of sergeant or warrant officer, did not have such personal files.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have a look at the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see the personal file for Stipo Tomic continued.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Here we see the record of the time he spent in various units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it seems that in the B/C/S version that we often have two pages on -- two hard copy pages on one page, whereas the English takes them one by one. Could you please take care that we always look at the same, both in the original and in the English translation. Because if you want us to look at this, then we should go, I take it, one page forward in English --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, it would then be on page 4, I think, in English. Now they are corresponding again, it looks ... Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need right-hand side in next -- yeah, and next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rodic, not everything was translated. Kindly read out for us the dates and information for this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: In order to navigate the pages correctly, you can see the left-hand side column all the way at the left, and it says number 12, data on war-time assignments. This is where the unit and rank is entered for the person whose personal file this is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the last two sentences, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We should go back. We should go back one page. Actually, to left-hand side in B/C/S and previous page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. Rodic. We had a different thing on the screen. So column 12, what does it explain?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: War-time assignment, his position in it, and the mobilisational assembly point where he had to report if mobilised. It could also be used for military exercises. It wasn't necessary that it was only used in a time of war. There were also exercises carried out by the JNA and such information was entered here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now if we can move to the right-hand side in B/C/S and the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, not everything has been translated. Could you just briefly read for us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page, actually, in English. The next page. One page further. It looks like this is continuation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In which language one page further, Mr. -- in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there we are. Number 14 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are now on the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, what can we see here under 14?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: This is promotion. We see that once a soldier leaves the school for reserve officers, he is automatically promoted into a reserve officer. His first rank was the second lieutenant. And then after the exercises in the JNA, it was possible to be further promoted and move up the ranks. You can see how this person was promoted and in what years. So second lieutenant, lieutenant captain, captain first class, and finally major in 1989. This is the promotion record of this person Tomic whose personnel file this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we were looking at the previous page, did you manage to establish what the ethnicity of this person Tomic is?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we go back to the second page, please, in B/C/S. And it would be the third page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Column 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need right-hand side in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In B/C/S, it's the wrong page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just move it to the right, please. Yes, now we are -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mention column 4.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, column 4 depicts his nationality as Croat and his social origin. He is described as a peasant or a worker.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it customary for these personnel files to show a person's ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. The ethnicity is recorded in both the personnel files and the unit files for all the unit members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification. If looks as if the word "hrvat" is stricken through and that there is some handwriting under it. Can you read that, Witness? And could you tell us what it says? Do you have any explanation as to why it is stricken through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, there's the word "Yugoslav" underneath, which means that in the former state of Yugoslavia, people were allowed to state their ethnicity as Yugoslav. That started some ten years before the war. The citizens were allowed to state their ethnicity as Yugoslav. Stipo Tomic corrected his ethnicity, and I can see that there is a date next to that, and there must be a stamp to confirm that correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least the transcription is incomplete in this respect, the English, because it doesn't reflect the handwriting. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would offer this document and we don't mind, if my learned friend has some questions, to postpone the admission until the end, but this is the gentleman whose -- through whose organisation we acquired those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just two quick clarifications before articulating a positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no problem that these questions are put --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to the witness now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: They were actually clarifications for Mr. Lukic. First, whether he is seeking to rely on all of the personnel records that are part of this bundle or just the one that's been used. And second, whether the translation issue that the Bench just identified is going to be corrected before admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can MFI. Of course, we are ready to correct whatever we have to correct. And we would want all -- it's not bundle. I think it's only four for three people. I can go through all of them but it would take more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it looks as if there are two under this number, isn't it? The first --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Next is Mr. Drincic, Niko; and the third one is Hodzic, Nesib.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's the -- the column --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which page in English? Yes, I see that apparently they are shorter or they are different or -- but I see that there are three persons and you want to rely on?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All of them because one is Yugoslav, one is Croat, the third one is Muslim, so that's why we need all three of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, did you receive the information you needed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have. And I think we're in agreement that it remain MFI'd pending the translation issue. I -- I was seeking clarification but wasn't requesting Mr. Lukic go through all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Since there's now a translation issue, we'll formally MFI it under the number already assigned to it. Madam Registrar, that's put on the record hereby. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, you did not activate your microphone. I think you were referring to the number, but perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's D768.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, is marked for identification. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And the next document we need on our screens is D769.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that also MFI'd?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Actually, it was not admitted because we said we will bring the gentleman through whom we received those documents, and this is exactly Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's understood. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Again, we have the same page. We made three copies thereof. We need to look at the second page of the document, or rather we need page 4 in B/C/S, which is probably more legible. I assume that the corresponding page in the English version will -- would also be page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, before us we have the unit record. What is that? Can you explain? This is the unit record for Stefo Brisevac.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I told you, the first bundle of files is only for officers, and this unit record, personnel record for the unit, refers to everybody else. At the moment, we are in possession of some 26.000 of such unit record for individuals in the army. Those records started when recruitment started in the former system. From then on, the unit or personnel record for the unit contains all the relevant information for each particular soldier, his speciality, a change in the unit status, a change in the place of residence, or -- and all the other relevant data that need to be entered into the record. That record starts its life when it is established that a person has reached military age. As far as our department is concerned, I found the oldest record which dates -- or rather, the information in the record being the year 1905. Our obligation is to keep -- keep this record for 70 years from the date they were created. These records are public information accessible to the public on request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this also something that is your base for information provided to the prosecutor's office in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the courts?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. These records are often requested by the prosecutor's office, but we also have cases when such records are requested when a person applied for dual citizenship or the issuance of a passport. For example, in Croatia a person may be asked to provide this unit record in order to prove that they had served in the army. That's very often necessary when a person applies for a second citizenship. And then under 7, nationality or ethnicity, this is to prove what the person's previous ethnicity or nationality was. In other words, when a person comes and requests a certificate based on this personnel record, the purpose has to be stated. For example, the purpose may be the issuance of a passport, of dual citizenship, or the citizenship of a third country. All such records or information based thereupon can be requested by an official government body for their purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I need a guidance now. Are we working in one-hour sessions or we -- since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I would like to go back to the usual sessions of one hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we need D896, which has been MFI'd. And I would tender the previous one into evidence as well, D769.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, I may have brief questions about it, and I'd just ask to reserve my position until I've asked them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That request is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, we have a document before us. Its title is a list of conscripts. Do you see it on the screen, and can you read it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "1, list of conscripts, Croats, 381."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I seek clarification about the name which appears in the English translation on the right-hand side. We see there the name Miso Radic. I take it this is a mistranslation, if this was - and I would ask the witness - perhaps we could -- have to go to the last page in the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see the last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- to see the original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it says Radic, it's a mistake. It should be R-o, Rodic, not R-a, Radic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And is that your signature -- is it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbian version, it says Miso Rodic, which is correct. The signature is not mine. It belongs to the desk officer that I've already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And above the signature we see a handwritten entry with a name. And this refers to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says department chief, Miso Rodic. I am department chief. This is my position. And before that it say, "za," on behalf of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see my name handwritten, but the signature is that of the desk officer who is authorised to sign such documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, how did you compile this list, or rather several lists: One for Croats, another one for Bosniaks, a third one for Slovenians, and so on and so forth? What procedure did apply to identify those people by ethnicity. How was this list compiled?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: What we saw in the previous documents, i.e., personnel records for all the soldiers, were copied electronically. They contain all the different data which are contained in the personal records of all the soldiers. At the request of the Defence, we programmed the computer to bundle up together people of particular ethnicity. I believe that you remember column 4 or 7 and 8, which also depicts ethnicity. The computer basically recognised those columns as separate columns and bundled up the ethnicities together. This was done at your request.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the records, is there more information or is this all the information?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The records contain more information. The records also contain information about military exercises, about movement through units. For example, Stipo Tomic attended some 10 or 15 exercises. There is a record of his joining the unit, when he was demobilised, on what grounds, and so on and so forth. This information is not contained here. The way we understood the Defence's request was that we should submit a list of participants in the war who were not Serbs; in other words, Croat, Muslim or Bosniak, Slovenian, Ukrainian, the Roma ethnicity, so on and so forth. Based on that request, we have programmed our computer to come up with the list that you can now see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can this register also be verified?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, if officially requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This kind of record was created and kept by your department. Why was it necessary to do so? How is it used by the citizens?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: When we used this record, we also check the physical documents, the unit records we saw. However, we used this as a tool to speed up the process. For example, if there is Ivo Antic requesting something, we type his name into the computer and we get the data listed, enabling us to quickly access all the other data pertaining to his person -- to his service. We look at the files and the end result of the process is a certificate requested by Ivo Antic for whatever purpose. It is also very useful for statistics. It is, of course, much easier to do so via a PC. We had your specific request to come up with the list of people of different ethnicities. In other words, computer entry enables us to go through the database much more quickly than we otherwise would be able to by hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under veteran's rights, what kind of rights can be exercised by the people on these lists?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: They all have the same rights. Ethnicity is not a pre-condition. The pre-condition is their participation in the war. A demobilised veteran receives an annual sum for fighters or former fighters until they are 60 years old. When they pass that age, it is converted to a monthly instalment and then they receive monthly veteran's payments. If there was any wounding or damage to their body, they also have the disability amount. If the person was killed, his family has the right to his military pension. All that is not pre-conditioned in any way by ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness tell us -- or perhaps, Mr. Lukic, are you going to pay the attention to the last column, the date of status?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is exactly what I wanted to ask him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I'll refrain from --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, I asked you about the last column since it wasn't clear to me. What does it mean, "date of status"?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: In the processing of the unit files, we keep going back and forth to harmonise data. As long as the ministry in -- existed, there was communication between local secretariats and the central database at the ministry. If you recall, I mentioned decisions necessary to be able to enter any changes. When the last change is entered in a file, that date is considered date of status. It doesn't mean the date when the file was created but the date of the last amendment in the file or when the last -- when the data was checked last. We see that most of these dates go up to 2005, which is for as long as the ministry existed. Any subsequent changes were very rare and only happened in such cases when the interested party was successful in obtaining a decision from the ministry or was in another way involved in legal proceedings requesting any changes. So this actually means the last change entered in either a personal or unit file. Let me add this: These changes needn't be physical. In other words, it could also mean that we made classifications according to military specialties, and that was the date of status. In other words, the file remained intact but only the date was changed, although no change was requested. For example, it could have been part of a procedure to verify or check all background data, and that date would then be entered as the date of status. It is a purely administrative piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, thank you. This was all we had for you at this moment. And thank you for answering our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one question. Mr. Rodic, the list, as it is now before us, that is, the list with the various ethnically split-up conscripts, does that give any information as to whether or not they were serving in -- between 1991 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see there were 381 Croats here. All of them were members of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we start with the 16th of September, all 381 are registered in the VOB-8 we saw at the very beginning of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's not an answer to my question. My question is whether on the basis of what we see before us, whether that can tell us anything about their membership of the army or activities in that context during the period 1991-1995. And let me clarify your [sic] question. If someone would have joined the VRS in 1997, would he be on this list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We tasked the computer, upon the Defence request, to come up with the people out of the 26- or the 27.000 people who met two conditions: One, was participation in the war; two, was that they were -- are of non-Serb ethnicity. As per that request, the computer came up with this information. All that information could be seen in the individual files of each and every name we see on the list. In those files, unit files, you can also find information in terms of what unit and what position they were in. Had the Defence been more detailed in their request, the result would have contained information about the dates between someone who was part of a particular unit. We can also provide that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you receive that request in writing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you still have it, or is the Defence still having it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My investigator, Mitrovic, sent the request, so I'm sure he has it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you still have a copy, Witness, of the request as given to you in writing by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so. If I recall well, when we looked at VOB-8s, on the cover page it said pursuant to your request number so-and-so, if I'm correct. We could see it on the cover page when you asked me about my signature, and I said then that it was signed by the authorised desk clerk. We referenced the Defence request for information. Otherwise, we would not have been in a position to forward it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's, I think, not on this list, but I have a recollection that I've seen that a reference was made to a request. Could you -- if you have it, could you please keep it. Well, Mr. Lukic, if you would be in a position to provide a copy to the Chamber, then we would know exactly what we see before us, because the printout doesn't give the information I was asking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that's the -- on that list, could be only someone who was a member of either VJ or VRS. Nobody else could be on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that was not my question. It was about war experience. And that's, of course, different from being a VRS member. Apparently, as the witness explained to us, a further selection was made as to who had served during war time and who did not, but that -- those data, that information, is not in this printout of this database.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- if I just may clarify with the witness or if you can ask --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, in this register, can we find anyone who did not participate in the war?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. The computer worked on the basis of two tasks. One was to take all those participating in the war who were fighters of the VRS or previously of the JNA. So those were the two. You cannot find a name in the VOB-8 of someone who was not in a particular unit during the war. There's information for each and every person in terms of where they were at what time. The list of 381 contains only such people. You do not have information about the dates, that is true, but they had all participated in the war. It must be so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Well, whether it is or whether it must be so, these are two different things, but I understand that you say there were only those who served during war time are in this database or is on the VOB-8. Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock. We could do two things, start for five minutes your cross-examination or take a break first.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm in the Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I'm more or less soliciting what your preference would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Then I'm happy to start, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll start. Mr. Rodic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution, and you'll most likely see him soon on your screen. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I have a few questions about the documents we just looked at. Now, one of the statuses that's listed for some of the servicemen in D896, which I noticed you did not mention on direct when you were listing the different statuses, is translated as: "Moved out, non-Serbs." Why is there a specific category for non-Serbs who moved out of the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I presume you had in mind the reason why that person was taken off the list in the register. There was a description in terms of why that person moved out. In other words, there was no official request. Rather, an instruction must have existed. Such changes at the time were carried out by the Ministry of Defence of Republika Srpska, so I did not read any such instructions. I do suppose, however, that all such terms were with the Ministry of Defence because they always worked strictly to standard procedure. You could find there the reasons why somebody was taken out of that register. I don't know why it says "non-Serb," but I presume it was per instructions of someone in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're aware that about 15 per cent of the Muslims and about the same percentage of the Croats in this list are listed as having moved out of Prijedor municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I could take each individual unit file to check that information. I don't know personally. I may be aware of some examples, but these people were then my friends. I do suppose, however, that is all in the registers. If you're interested in anyone in particular and if you lodge an official request, we can come up with that person's individual file where you can see all that information. What you see before you is a public document and it remains to be so for the time being. It is based on the assumption of truthfulness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you to focus carefully on the question I ask you. I understand that your answer to my last question was that you are not, at this moment, sure if it's right that about 15 per cent and about -- of the Muslims and about 15 per cent of the Croats on this list moved out of Prijedor. Have I correctly understood your answer?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this document won't show when they moved out of Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I tried to explain that. We provided excerpts from registers. This excerpt before you does not contain that information, but there is information in existence for each and every person individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And those Muslims and Croats listed in this document as having moved out, non-Serbs, were part of, of course, thousands, tens of thousands of non-Serbs who moved out of Prijedor municipality during the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. People moved out and they were a part of that movement. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you said this document starts on the 16th of September, 1991. That means that, in principle, if someone served in the JNA from the 16th to the 18th of September, 1991, and never served in the VRS at all, they would be on this list; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. If it was noted as war participation. I think at the time such information was also kept for the conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you mentioned with regard to one of the other documents that a sample was provided. Who selected which samples from the VOB would be provided?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I suppose the authorised desk clerk did. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you -- so you don't know yourself which persons are or are not included in the version of the VOB that has been provided to this Court, do you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I know it was provided and I know that I authorised that provision, but that is the extent of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the time-period in question starts on the 16th of September, 1991, because that's when there was a mobilisation in Prijedor at JNA direction into units that were deployed to Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we're now at the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are, Mr. Traldi. Witness, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I would like to deal with a matter very briefly in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could the witness be escorted into the videolink courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have MFI D767, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this, again, is the cover of the portion of the VOB we've received. Sir, I have just a couple of additional questions about it. We see this runs up to the 30th of March, 1996. So the VOB would certainly include records of people who were only mobilised after all the fighting in Prijedor was over; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. This VOB runs up to the 30th of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If somebody was mobilised, for instance, or joined the army on the 29th of March, 1996, would they be included?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. However, with a reservation. We were not the ones who compiled those lists. These lists are only kept as records in our department. I don't know how they were compiled. I cannot testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 3 in the B/C/S only, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you testified that this is a sample, and so I just want to look quickly at the start and the end. We see this starts at person number 243; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, Ljubomir Aramanda.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see the last record on this page is number 258.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we turn to the next page, page 4 in the B/C/S only.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The first record is 434. The portion of the VOB including, for instance, the brigade commander in 1992, Colonel Arsic, has not been included, has it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could turn just to the very end, page 36 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see the very last name, and that's Dragan Soldat. Now the book is in alphabetical order --

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Soldat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The book's in alphabetical order, so nobody whose name comes after Dragan Soldat in the alphabet is included in the sample that we have; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. I can only testify about the fact that this is the accurate copy of the original. As the chief of the relevant department, I can testify to that. Now, as to how the list was originally compiled and when and the procedure that was followed, I can't testify about that because I was not a participant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Were you part of making this copy?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Nenad Babic, who is also authorised to provide information based on military record, did that on my order. I was informed about the Defence request. I approved that request. I knew what the Defence requested. The VOB books are very heavy and voluminous. They weigh over 10 kilos, if this means anything to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: It would have been very hard to copy them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, do I correctly understand that you did not participate in making the copy yourself; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness is -- cannot hear us obviously right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He already answered that he did not do that, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we can offer now, we can offer the whole registry if the Prosecution wants. What we tried to do is to cut down the number of pages. We can easily acquire the whole list and we are very happy to provide it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the basis for the selection? That apparently is the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we let that guy to copy whatever he wants. The employee of the same institution. So if he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your position is clear, Mr. Lukic. You are ready to request -- to be provided with the full 10 kilos, if I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if Your Honours order us to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And this Chamber knows what 10 kilo is. There's no doubt about that. Witness, you may have answered the question but the videolink connection was interrupted. Therefore, Mr. -- we have as an answer -- let me just see. No, you have -- we have no answer yet. Mr. Traldi will repeat his last question to you and then you're invited to answer that. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, do I correctly understand that you did not participate in making this copy yourself; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: You understood me properly. I did not participate in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you check it against official records?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I did, one part. Since I had been informed that some dates were missing from the records; namely, the dates when people joined the unit and when they left the unit. I checked that. We have that information, but I am personally not authorised to submit that information to you if you don't request it. I personally checked that that information exists for every individual and that that information can be provided for every individual upon somebody's request; i.e., the information on the duration of their service in a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just two more questions. We see Dragan Soldat is the last name. Now, in alphabetical order, we would expect Dragomir Soldat to appear on the very next page; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: This is the last entry. I don't know what follows, what's on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you know Dragomir Soldat was a soldier in the 43rd Brigade, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is part of the VOB of the 43rd Brigade. So all people in this book were members of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he, if we had the next page, if it'd included his name, it would reflect him, and you also know he was recently convicted in Bosnia for massacring a group of Muslim civilians in front of the Carakovo mosque in July of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to your own positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm done with this document unless Their Honours have any questions on it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have no questions at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now before I ask about your positions during the war, I understand this is the first time you're testifying at the Tribunal. You were, however, interviewed by Radovan Karadzic's Defence team; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Indeed, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were you aware they produced a draft statement on the basis of that interview?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you review that draft statement?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I believe that we left it with a promise that they would send me that draft, but they never did because they never intended to call me as a witness. In other words, I never had an opportunity to review the draft version of that statement because they decided not to call me as a witness. I only assumed that that version is accurate, but I never checked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And are you aware whether it was used as a basis for your Mladic statement?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I provided the statement based on the questions that were put to me. That statement never came up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, one matter still remains unclear to me. That draft statement taken, did you ever see that draft statement? Did the witness hear my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I thought you were addressing the Prosecutor, not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I was --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did -- When the statement was drafted, I read it. I glanced at it. But I didn't have enough time to review it. Then I was promised that the full draft would be sent to me. That never transpired because they decided not to call me as a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to your wartime positions. Now, you were an officer in the intelligence and security organ of the 43rd Motorised Brigade. Who was the head of intelligence and security in the 43rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic while I was there, and the Lieutenant Toric for a while as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Was it Lieutenant-Colonel Miroslav Majstorovic who would issue you your tasks?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know who he reported to?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: He was an assistant commander of the brigade. I know that the intelligence had its hierarchy that went in parallel with the brigade because they reported to the regiment in the 1st Krajina Corps. And that was done unbeknownst to the brigade commander, because they worked along a separate line of responsibility and reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So he would report at first on his work to Colonel Stevilovic and then to Colonel Bogojevic, the assistant commanders for intelligence and security at the 1st Krajina Corps level; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I know that in the security organ there was that direct line of reporting, which bypassed the superior commander. Whether he communicated with the two persons that you have mentioned, there's no way for me to know that because those messages were encrypted and I can't testify about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you would report on your work to him; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was more closely linked to security, which was not my part of work. But as intelligence, we were part of a joint organ, and he was the assistant commander for both security and intelligence. Very often in practice the intelligence we received would have ended up with the Chief of Staff in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So the Chief of Staff in the brigade at the relevant time, that's Radmilo Zeljaja; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, Radmilo Zeljaja.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we're talking about the intelligence you received, we're talking, in part, about the results of the interrogations you conducted; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Some of the intelligence was obtained through interrogation. There were also other methods to collect intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you would provide the results of the interrogations to Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were regular briefings at which we briefed him about all that. But we also had frequent contacts --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The connection is too bad for interpretation. Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you're being asked to repeat your last answer. Just to assist, I'll ask the question again. The question had been: You provided the results of the interrogations to Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were recorded to say there were regular briefings at which you briefed him about all of that. That means you briefed him regularly about the results of the interrogations you conducted; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And before the interpreters stopped being able to hear you, you'd started to explain: "... we also had frequent contacts..." Who were you about to tell the Trial Chamber you also had frequent contacts with?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so would you also provide him, in practice, with the results of the interrogations you conducted?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. Only the information which were of some importance for the use of the unit was highlighted. For example, the information about the enemy that may have led to certain decisions on the use of our own unit. We did not provide the entire information that derived from the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Where was your office during this period?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: As far as I recall, for the initial fortnight it was in the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks in the building that housed the personnel service, given that there was a lack of space. Later on we moved to the administrative building of the Prijedor Putevi or Kozara Putevi company, as one leaves Prijedor en route to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Chamber has received evidence that in the summer of 1992, the command of the 43rd Brigade moved into that building. Which members of the command had offices in the Kozara Putevi building at that time?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can say with certainty that there was an organ for morale; that is to say, assistant commander for morale. There was assistant commander for intelligence and security. I think, in terms of logistics, they remained at the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Where was Colonel Arsic at this time?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: In the Prijedor Putevi or Kozara Putevi building, depending on what you want to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 32004.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what you're going to see in front of you on your screen and what we're seeing on ours is an aerial image of the part of Prijedor where the Kozara Putevi building was located. I understand, due to the videolink --

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- we'll -- I'll have to ask you to describe, but can you describe on this building the location of the Kozara Putevi building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness first identify the building, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm -- on this, you mean on the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we understood "on this building," which -- a building which was not yet identified, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Because I said that mistakenly. I'll reword the question, if Your Honours don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, looking at this image, first, do you see the Kozara Putevi building?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you describe for us where that building is on this image.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can. Let us look from the same angle. If we have the R number in the upper right-hand side corner, if you follow the main road on the right towards the middle of the picture, there is a turn to the right, which is clearly visible. At that intersection, there's first a building with a red roof and then behind it is a building with a blue roof. The red-roofed building is the building of the Prijedor Putevi company. Behind it is a large parking-lot where they kept their equipment, their machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what's the large building with the grey roof across the street from it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: It is Keraterm. I think you have information about it and that there is no need for me to explain anything in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I won't have any questions about it for you at this moment, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: But I would tender the image, 65 ter 32004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not still entirely certain that I understand what the witness told us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I -- because there seems to be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's still some confusion. Could I take you step by step. We start where the large red letter R is; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I now go to the left of that, we see that there's a main road which goes from the top to the bottom of this picture and is slightly bended; do you see that road? Now we --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move from the top of this picture slowly down along this road. You're still following me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you tell us where approximately is the red-roofed building you wanted to draw our attention to? Is that halfway from the top to the bottom? Is it at one-third?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it will be easy for you to navigate. If we start from the top of the photograph where you started and follow the main road, there's an intersection to the left and to the right. That is not the part I had in mind.
