You continue down to the -- towards the middle, and you will see another intersection going also to the left and to the right. The one that goes towards the red-roofed building is the entry to the Prijedor Putevi company. If one moves from top to bottom. I don't know how precise I was. It is somewhere around the middle of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I -- let me try to make sure that we fully understand you. So we moved down and you said there's an intersection to the left and to the right, another intersection going also to the left and to the right. And you say: "The one that goes towards the red-roofed building..." is that coming from the top --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the entry point to the Prijedor Putevi company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is that where we see -- one second. One second, please. Would you please wait for a second and try to answer my questions. You were talking about a red-roofed building. I see one red-roofed building which is -- with a small white striping in the middle of it; do you see that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but that is not where the command was. It was further down in one of the smaller buildings. The smaller building immediately adjacent to it that has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So we have two larger red-roofed buildings which are at an angle of 90 degrees in relation to each other. We have an area in the centre of that which from here it looks like there's some rubble but it's an open space. And then we have a smaller building, red-roofed, with what seems to be a number of cars between that building and that main road. Is that the building you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the other side of the road are two trees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't see those -- well, I do see two trees. Could I ask you one thing -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a picture or do you have it on your screen in the videolink room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just asking for some technical details. If we moved the cursor on our screen here, would that be visible on the other side? I think it's not. Madam Registrar, could you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yeah, we can hear you now. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] No, the witnesses won't be able -- uh-huh. The witness can see now. I don't know how sharp is that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Is there any way --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Can we put a small picture so that the witness can see the entire ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see. When we move our cursor, is that possible to move --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You see that cursor at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we move the cursor slightly to the right, is that the building you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think it's clear to all of us. Now how to put this on the record. Can a -- can a still be made with the cursor on it at this moment or is that impossible? A print screen with the cursor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it possible to make a marking here around that building and then ask the witness whether he sees it and whether it accurately ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, did you see the marking being made on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the building. Then I take it that this would be a Prosecution Exhibit, or would you like to have more markings?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just for the clarity of the record, if the Registry official could also circle the large grey-roofed building across the street, and then I'll ask the witness to confirm that that's the building he understood me to mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Than the one that the cursor is on now, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we'll make another marking on what we think you referred to as being the Keraterm building. Could you carefully look at the marking being made. What is marked now with a red oval. Is that the Keraterm building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the building of Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any further markings needed, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. And I thank Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you want to tender these marked images.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I would before we lose it, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned to this marked picture would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number would be P7203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you said after about a fortnight you moved there. So is it right that you began to be based in the Kozara Putevi building around the middle of June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. I don't recall the exact date. I do remember that we came a little before the rest of the command arrived. I don't know when exactly, but it is around the date you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How long did you continue to be based in the Kozara Putevi building?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: We stayed there until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Colonel Arsic -- you said you came a little before the rest of the command arrived. About how long after you arrived was it that Colonel Arsic began to be based in the Kozara Putevi building?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, some 15 to 20 days later. But that's what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So around the early part of July or the end of June 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat? The signal was too weak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've been asked to repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: In terms of your question, because you're asking me about the dates, I can say that I don't know. I can only -- you tried to use my memory but I'm not sure whether it was on this or that specific date. I'd rather not be specific. I can try to confirm your date, but I would rather say in June or July or, say, early summer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I hadn't asked for a specific date. When you say June or July, what I'd put to you is that it would be late June or early July, approximately; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I think you mentioned the 15th. In any case, as for the rest of what you said, it could be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I want to turn to the interrogations you conducted. Where did you conduct interrogations?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: At first for a short while it was in the personnel office of the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks, but it was only for a little while. Later on we used the premises of the military police, immediately outside the Keraterm compound. On this photograph there is a building in the back, somewhat smaller, and with a red roof which housed the military police, or rather some elements of it, including the crime investigation service. We frequently used that space for interrogations. In exceptional cases, say, in two or three case, we used the building of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Traldi, of course, we see approximately 25, 30, 40 houses with red roofs, so I leave it to you whether you want to further -- to have a further specification or that you are satisfied that it was somewhere in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say a building in the back, somewhat smaller, with a red roof is the building that house the military police. The back of what?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: If we start with the R number and move down to the Keraterm building, which we identified a moment ago, there is some reddish colour and a white line across it. This is where the offices were. It was an out-building of the Keraterm complex. It is that building that was used by the military police of the 43rd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now I see, sir, a reddish line on the roof at the right-most part of the Keraterm complex on this image. Is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, no. This is right in the middle of the building immediately after -- below the letter R. If you go down, there are first two roofs, and then you can just barely see a reddish roof rather unclearly. But it seems there's a dotted line of sorts going across that reddish part. It is close to the Keraterm compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Perhaps I've got it this time. If you were to come out the gate of Keraterm, there's a road just off the main road. Is it below that road on the image, what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the use of a cursor again not be helpful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. You have to follow the road to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to do the same as we did before. Could we have now the exhibit with the markings as a starting point and which has been stored. Could you now help us? The cursor should now go to the letter R. Could you give instructions --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now follow the road downwards. Go down by some 10 centimetres, vertically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where the R is there is no road downwards, but the cursor now moves now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue. Continue. More. More. More. Stop. Go slightly up. You went too far. Now to the right. A little bit. That's the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let me see. You say the building is now -- the cursor is a small object which goes from left down to right up. Is it at the upper side of where you see the cursor that you see the building? Because the lower part seems to be where Keraterm is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the part that is stable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we move up the cursor very slightly a little bit up. Little bit more. Little bit more. Little -- stop. Is now the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The part that is blinking is on the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see any blinking. But is it true that the cursor, which looks like a pen, that where the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The part closer to Keraterm is on top of the building -- of the roof of that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we mark that at this moment. Around that building of which the ... Is that marking the building you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the building which housed the military police of the 43rd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Traldi, any further marking needed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest, as a matter of fact, that we replace the previous marked aerial picture by this new one, the new one having three markings on it, rather than to have two exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the -- could you please repeat the number under which we admitted the previous marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number was P7203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you are hereby instructed to replace the previously marked aerial picture by the now newly marked with all three markings on it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, about -- oh. We were on interrogations. Who would bring people to you to be interrogated?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: As a rule, the military police did if we issued them with an order to bring someone. When the units were being formed around June 1992, the security organs of those subordinate battalion-level units were included in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you didn't conduct the interrogations alone; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. It never happened that only one officer interrogated. There was always a policeman present for security reasons and another colleague. For the most part, it was Captain Stevica and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say a policeman, you mean somebody from public security?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. We had an MP company in the brigade that was in charge of performing such tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And there were two other teams of interrogators at that facility; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to intelligence interrogations, also security organs were involved. They mostly relied on a crime investigation platoon that they had as part of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And one of the military policemen who would participate was a man named Dragan Radetic; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I know Dragan Radetic personally, and he was, indeed, a member of the military police. I think that we participated in perhaps only two interrogations, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you refer to the interrogations of several specific person information your statement. Asking you for now about Sead Cirkin, where was he detained when he was brought to you to be interrogated?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I know that Sead Cirkin was taken prisoner by the Dubica Brigade. We received information from them that he was an officer from Kozarac and that we should come and take him over because he was from our area, and we were supposed to continue his processing. He was brought to the building of the command for interrogation. I have already told you that on two or three occasions the interrogations took place at the command building. One of such cases was the case of Mr. Sead Cirkin. I don't know where he was actually kept in custody and where they actually brought him from and where then they returned him to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You refer to an Asim Muhic. He was a detainee at Keraterm at the time that you interrogated him; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't think that information is correct. Muhic was in the detention part of the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks together with the members of the VRS who were serving some disciplinary measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to turn from that to a specific member of the VRS. You refer in paragraph 26 of your statement to an investigation into Zoran Zigic. Now, Mr. Zigic was convicted at this Tribunal after the war of war crimes and crime against humanity. You're aware of that today. Right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know Zoran Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the investigations into him that you refer to in the summer of 1992, those investigations were, first, for taking a bribe; and second, for a crime of robbery, right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I did not follow the investigation of Zoran Zigic. I never spoke to him about that. I was present once he was arrested, and then he was taken into the same detention where Muhic was. I never took any statements from Zigic. This was more within the purview of the security part of our service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So in paragraph 26 of your statement when you say that you can confirm with certainty that the military police of the Prijedor garrison took appropriate measures in accordance with its competences concerning the investigation into crimes committed by members of the VRS against Muslims and Croats, and you refer to the investigation in the case of Zoran Zigic, in fact, you were not involved in that investigation, took no statements, and do not know what crimes he was being investigated for. Is that your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can't answer just by a "yes" or "no." I said that at first I was also working as a legal expert in the Department for Morale. So penal policy and the rest of it was what I did. I would have to deal with the qualification of a crime and instigating procedure against the perpetrator. Statements were taken from that person during the investigation and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that's a very long answer. Could you tell us where you say that the investigations carried out in the cases of Zoran Zigic, whether you knew what these investigations were about as far as the crimes involved are concerned? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that one was looting or robbery. I participated in that arrest. However, I was not involved in the taking of his statement or I did not witness the moment when he pleaded guilty to that crime, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the only thing you know is that when you arrested him it was for robbery. Is that well understood? And -- looting and robbery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was present during that robbery. I heard rumours of other kind from various sources, but that's a different story.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Who were the victims of this robbery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Muslims in Gomjenica, which is a suburban settlement of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the name of the settlement was Ganici or something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you have answered my question. Thank you. Please, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, as to the rumours that you heard, one of the rumours that you heard was that he'd previously been arrested and then had been released; right? At the time that you arrested him for robbery.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was remanded in custody for a short while. He was of an excellent behaviour while he was in custody. But as soon as he was released, he returned to his old ways and continued with the commission of misdeeds.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32194.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see this is a document from Dusko Knezevic, Sergeant Dusko Knezevic, and it begins by referring to information that: "... our soldier, Zoran Zigic, was detained for a criminal act set out in Article 230, paragraph 1, ..." Now, you said a moment ago that you'd served as a legal expert. Article 230, do you recall what that is?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I'm not familiar with this document either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was not whether you're familiar with the document but whether you could tell us what Article 230, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Code stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the parties agree on what it stands for? Mr. Lukic, you would --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We can speak at the break on that, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you said a moment ago that he was of an excellent behaviour while he was in custody. If we read further in this document, we read that Sergeant Knezovic says: "We're addressing you because," beginning on the third line in the English, "our sabotage and reconnaissance unit is getting ready to go to the front in Derventa, probably on Sunday 12 July 1992. As Zoran Zigic is a very capable, obedient and a diligent fighter-soldier, and one of best experts on explosive, we ask, legal framework permitting, that he would be freed from detention. We personally guarantee that he shall be made available for the eventual trial when the time comes for that." So the truth is he wasn't released from custody because of excellent behaviour. He was released because Sergeant Knezovic requested that he be released so he could go back to his unit and go to the front; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think that I ever said that he was released because he was a model prisoner. I just said that he was well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The answer was not completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we found 1, 2 -- 230, Article 230.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We found what Article 230 was at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but you also interrupted the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's an unlawful abandonment of a front line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Does that ring a bell to you, Witness, that Article 230 is unlawful abandonment of a front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I do have a degree in law, but I'm not -- I don't know all the articles by heart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please continue your answer. You said you don't think that you ever said that he was released because he was a model prisoner. And then you said: "I just said that he was well ..." And what did you then say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When he was being arrested, he behaved exceptionally well. He was a model prisoner, that is true. But that was not the reason why he was released from custody, nor I do know when that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32196.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a decision by the Prijedor Lower Court dated the 9th of July, 1992. We see that Zigic is hereby released from custody. And below that in the third paragraph below statement of reasons, we read: "Added in the file is also an information which shows the necessity for the accused to be engaged in the Zoran Karlica unit as an excellent and capable worker-soldier who is knowledgeable about explosives." Now, the Zoran Karlica Unit, that was the sabotage and reconnaissance unit of the 43rd Brigade that at this point was commanded by Dusko Knezevic; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what I'm putting to you, sir, is that when you say the military police investigated Zigic, what happened was he was released at the request of his commander to go back to his unit and go back to the front. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: If I have looked at this carefully, people were remanded in custody at Zarko Zgonjanin barracks on the order of the commander of the 43rd Brigade. As far as I can remember, Zivko Dragasevac was a judge of the court in Prijedor. If I'm not mistaken, the basic court in Prijedor. So this is a completely different matter. I'm talking about the time when Zigic was remanded in custody because of the disciplinary measure instituted by the brigade commander. This is something else. This is a -- this is proceedings before a regular basic court of which I know nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, first, at this point he would initially have been arrested by the military police because he was a soldier; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So this first arrest the chain also begins with the military police arresting him, and it ends with him being released on the request of his commander; correct?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. You're actually mixing up two different and wrong things. My answer is no. The commander did not have any authority before the basic court in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, Zigic was in the Zoran Karlica Unit. The commander of it was Dusko Knezevic at this time. We've just seen Knezevic requesting him to be released. We've just seen -- in fact, we're looking now at the decision releasing him which refers, in part, to the request from his commander. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can read this in the statement of reasons of the court in Prijedor. I don't know whether this is truth -- the truth or not. I can only cite the document. I can give you all the figures and all the facts, but this is not the thing that I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn to his second arrest in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I do, I'd tender 65 ter 32195 and 32196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, I apologise. 32194 and 32196.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32194 receives number P7204. And 32196 receives number P7205.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7204 and P7205 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32199.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is the arrest you're referring to when Zigic and Dosen -- or the arrest you were referring to a moment ago when Zigic and Dosen were detained for robbery; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I suppose that they were involved in -- with several robberies. I only know of one which took place in Gomjenica in the settlement of Ganici. That's the one I know of. If this is what this refers to. But this is the military court in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see that they, again, are releasing Zigic from detention; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that. I did not remand him in custody. I did not release him. I was never at the military court myself. Why are you asking me about the military court? How can I testify about that? I can only make up things. I really don't understand you. There is a basic court, a military court, and I had nothing whatsoever to do with any of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. You don't have to ask why questions are put to you. You should answer them to the best of your abilities. By the way, the reason Mr. Traldi is asking is because your referring to investigations against Zigic and Dosen and that's the reason why he explores it. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to be clear, Mr. Zigic was never convicted and sentenced during the war for any of his many crimes against Muslims and Croats, was he?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender 65 ter 32199.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't object but I think that this witness is not the proper witness to introduce this document through him. He had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He has -- the witness has -- in his statement has referred to an investigation against Zigic and Dosen, and in that respect this is relevant and probative. And even if the witness himself cannot say anything about the document, on the standard practice of this Chamber, that makes it admissible at this moment. Any other objections, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No other, except that he has no knowledge about this document at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you know what I refer to the constant practice of this Chamber in this respect. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32199 receives number P7206.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you referred to the robbery committed by Zigic that you know -- knew of as having taken place in the settlement of Ganici in Prijedor. Do you remember who the victim was?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I've already answered. Muslims. In Ganici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If I suggested it might have been a Hasnija Ganic, would that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know any of them by name. I am only aware of the case and the arrest. I had no contact whatsoever with the victims of that robbery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber's received evidence that by late summer 1992, the command of the 43rd Brigade and the 1st Krajina Corps command were aware that the Zoran Karlica Unit, in which Zigic was a soldier, had committed serious crimes, including crimes in Carakovo village. Were you aware of those crimes committed by members of Zigic's unit?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can't answer the first part of your question, about the command and whether the command was aware, because I was not a member of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask you if the command was aware. I asked you if you were aware. I told you the Chamber has already received evidence that the command knew.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the Chamber received. I don't know whether I can trust your words when you're speaking on behalf of the Chamber. I suppose that I should trust the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Be my guest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just answer the question. That's good enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please rephrase your question or clarify so I will answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whether you were aware of those crimes committed by members of Zigic's unit as described by Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When it comes to the crimes committed around Carakovo, I know of them partly from rumours. I directly did not participate in them, and I cannot testify about the crimes that were committed there. I know that there were rumours about those crimes. I know that crimes had been committed in and around Carakovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you were aware but have you no further knowledge. If would you have told us that right away, then we would have moved on more quickly. If there's -- if it ever comes to your mind again whether can you trust Mr. Traldi, just leave it to the Defence of Mr. Mladic and to this Chamber to find out whether Mr. Traldi, as is not what he usually does, is misleading you as a witness. So refrain from any comment on that and listen carefully to the next question. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're not aware of any investigation into those crimes in Carakovo that you heard about, are you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am about to turn to a new topic. I see we're very close to the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would have, however, one other question. Witness, you told us that the robbery for which you arrested Mr. Zigic was committed against Muslims. At the same time, you say you -- you never talked to the victims. What do you know about those robberies, especially in view of your knowledge that they were committed against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me describe a very specific event. We received a report that a member of the VRS had arrested two people and kept them in the elementary school. That person objected to the robbery that had been committed. When arrived there, we found Zigic and another soldier there and that third soldier, who was standing with a machine-gun at the entrance to the school because he was afraid that somebody similar to Zigic would come and set them free. When we arrived, he removed his weapon, he allowed us to enter, he handed over the two people who were arrested, and he was very visibly angry that they had taken certain things from the civilian. I found on the -- on the soldier that was standing next to Zigic some rings and other jewellery. Zigic was very disciplined. As soon as we arrived, he lowered his arms, surrendered, and we accompanied him to be remanded in custody at the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks, which was a military detention unit. That's how I know about the robbery that he had committed. I was not involved in any further interrogations or investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you have not answered my question because I was asking specifically on what your knowledge was based, that Muslims had been the victims of the robbery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found some necklaces in the pocket of the soldier who had been co-perpetrator together with Zigic, and also based on the statement of the soldier who had kept them in custody there in that elementary school who told us that they had committed that robbery in the village of Ganici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was those who had committed the robbery that told you that it was committed against persons living in the village of Ganici? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. It was the third soldier who had arrested them, because he objected to what they had done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And he told you that the robbery had been committed against persons living in the village of Ganici. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And every single inhabitant of that hamlet was of Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how do you know that every single inhabitant was of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about some six or seven households. The dwellers share the same family name, Ganic. Ganic is a Muslim family name. The number of the houses there was very small. That's how I conclude that all the inhabitants of the hamlet were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Traldi, is that the same name as you put to the witness? Is that -- is my recollection accurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We take a break. Could I inquire with the parties -- before I give an opportunity to Mr. Tieger to address us, could I inquire as to how much time? Let's just assume that we start again at 1.00. How much time would you still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I'm roughly on schedule, so I will need another half-hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would that be sufficient time, approximately the half-hour, a little bit over half an hour, for you, Mr. Lukic, to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it would, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then before we take a break -- we'll take a break soon, Witness, and we'd like to see you back at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. With respect to the matter the Court inquired about in private session, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Tieger. We take a break, and we resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although we still see on our screen that the far end microphone is switched off, let's see whether that becomes any better if Mr. Traldi resumes his -- Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to apologise first. I quoted the wrong criminal act from -- since criminal acts were changed, criminal codes were changed, so it was not abandonment of the front line, it was accepting the bribe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Accepting the bribe.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I discussed it with Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's good that you considered this during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're ready to continue, Mr. Traldi, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am. I understand we're agreed that the first arrest was for arrest for accepting a bribe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just very briefly on the last issue we were discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 32198.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is another decision from the Banja Luka Military Court. Looking at the decision we see Mladen Dosen, that his appeal has been granted and he's being released from custody with immediate effect. Now, below the word "rationale" we see this is about a robbery crime under Article 150. He was arrested together with Zigic; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I can't provide that piece of information to you. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see under rationale, at the end of the paragraph, a reference -- it's quite unclear in the B/C/S, but the translators -- the interpreters had found that it looked like Hasnija Ganic. Now, that's the last name of the victims of Zigic's crime that you mentioned; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: There are some Ganics living outside the hamlet too, so I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And is this the Dosen that you refer to in your statement, Mladen Dosen?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I don't recall mentioning Dosen in my statement. Perhaps you can jog my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me put it to you this way for efficiency: You're not aware that Mladen Dosen, or any other Dosen in the 43rd Brigade, was convicted and sentenced during the war for crimes against non-Serbs, are you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32198.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 32198 receives number P7207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Witness, you told us about another person being arrested together with Zigic. Who was that other person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you say you don't recall any Dosen in your statement, but I'll read just one line, I think I did it before, that you said as examples of the military police of the Prijedor garrison taking appropriate measures, you referred -- you said: "For example, I can refer to investigations carried out in the cases of Zoran Zigic and Dosen also known as Djole and others." Could you tell us what the investigation against Djole, or Dosen, was about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that Mladen Dosen and the Dosen whose first name I couldn't recall, aka Djole, it could be Djordje, I don't think the two are the same people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not my question. My question was what you could tell us about the investigation carried out against Dosen also known as Djole.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated that some measures were taken. As a lawyer in the command, I was present when they were trying to come up with a way to prosecute Zigic and Djole, Dosen. I knew Zigic in person. As for Djole, Dosen, I only know his nickname, Djole, whereas, I don't know him. The command was looking for a way to prosecute them so as to have a civilian court competent to try them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Prosecute them for what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For Dosen, individually, I don't know, because I didn't take part in any measures. I know about Zigic. I know for Dosen that there were stories going around that he even killed people. I only know it from stories. I know him as a person who killed others. I think the secretary of the lower court in Prijedor was one of his victims, but those were just rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you are telling us that you can confirm with certainty that appropriate measures were taken, and you are giving an example of Dosen, also known as Djole, but you only know about rumours in relation to Dosen. That is I understand your testimony to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assert that measures were taken. I never asserted anything in terms of their conduct. I know only that the command undertook measures to discipline them, and I was consulted since I have a legal degree. That is what I know about the measures taken. I didn't go into the reasons why in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, what measures were taken against him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First, I was requested to visit the military court of the 1st Krajina Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not -- I'm asking not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- so as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking what you were supposed to do. I'm asking specifically what measures were taken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The intention was to bring them before a military court, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, again, I'm not asking what intentions you may have had. My question is what measures were taken against Dosen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what further measures were taken. I was only familiar with the procedure that had to do with initiating proceedings with a military or civilian court. As for any specific measures, there's nothing I can tell you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to that. So when you said I assert that measures were taken, you do not know what measures were taken. That's, in short, your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's note: Could the witness kindly repeat his answer. We did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, as short as you gave it a second ago. I had asked you what measure that -- that you do not know what measures were taken, whether that's correctly understood.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It isn't clear to me what you mean by "measures." What do you have in mind? I'll try to answer briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to turn to your evidence about detention facilities in Prijedor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32191.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you claim in your statement the word "camps" was not used for Trnopolje, Keraterm, and Omarska. This is a report from the 1st Krajina Corps command dated the 7th of September, 1992. If we could turn to page 2 in the English in the middle and 3 in the B/C/S at the top, we read that: "The SR government and the SR army Main Staff make the first moves on purpose in order to show the above-mentioned commissions their true intention to reach crisis solution through the peaceful negotiations." Now, first, the SR government, that refers to the government of the Republika Srpska; right? Sir, were you able to hear the question?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. I only heard the last sentence. It is clear it was a decision of the government of Republika Srpska, but I did not hear the question itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it refers not just to the government of Republika Srpska but to the -- the Main Staff of the army. That's the Main Staff commanded at the time by General Mladic; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: It should be so. Mladic commanded it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, below that -- sir, below that we see the move that the government and the Main Staff have decided to make: "The first 50 prisoners will be released from the Manjaca and Trnopolje LRZs some day soon." Now "LRZ" stands for prisoner of war camp; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that abbreviation. It seems to me you translated it correctly, but there's nothing I can testify to in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're never heard in your career in the security and intelligence organ the abbreviation LRZ for "Logor Ratnih Zarobljenika"?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I stand by my statement. We did not use the term "camp."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was not whether you used it. The question was whether you were familiar with this abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. And I don't think we received any such documents. At least not the ones I could see when I was giving my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- you had answered my question already. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm putting two things to you here, and I'm going to do them one at a time. First I'm putting to you that it is not credible, based on your wartime occupation, that you are not familiar this abbreviation. Your evidence just now is not the truth, is it?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: You have the right it assert whatever you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm putting it to you to invite you to comment. Do you have any explanation of how you could have avoided learning the common abbreviation for prisoner-of-war camp when you served in the security and intelligence organ during the war?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The organ's name was organ for security and intelligence. I was in the intelligence part of it and I was interested in the enemy. My role was to familiarise myself with the enemy. Security was not my remit. However, I still assert that I never came across the acronym LRZ, at least not in any of the documents that I could lay my hands on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was not limited to documents. Are you saying you'd never came across the acronym ever? Documents or no documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under no circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, sir, what I'm putting to you is what the 1st Krajina Corps is writing here is the truth: The people in Trnopolje were prisoners and it was a camp. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I cannot testify to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 32191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32191 receives number P7208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7208 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in this regard, you claim in paragraph 24 of your statement that Trnopolje was created as a result of the order of the Prijedor garrison command to leave a corridor open for the evacuation of civilians in the direction of Kozarac, Trnopolje at the time of combat activities in the wider area of Kozarac. You say the Trnopolje collection centre was the first to be visited by Doctors Without Borders, the Red Cross, and journalists. Just to be totally clear, you agree with me that those Red Cross and journalist visits did not take place for more than two months after the camp was created; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I think that assertion is more or less correct. I can't recall a date, given the fact that I personally provided security for one such delegation. I don't know whether it was the Doctors Without Borders or a different organisation, but in any case I escorted them when they went to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you referred to the evacuation of civilians from Kozarac. You're aware that thousands of Muslim civilians fled Kozarac at the time of the attack; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The numbers probably correspond to what you said. I know the corridor was used. I did not take part in the operation in Kozarac. But in terms of receiving information about the opening of a corridor for civilians, I received that information from Mr. Radmilo Zeljaja. That piece of information about the corridor came from the Chief of Staff, Mr. Zeljaja. I did not participate in the Kozarac operation there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you're aware that the civilians who were at Trnopolje had -- that were from Kozarac had nowhere to go back to because their homes had been destroyed; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. The only information I received after that, given the fact that the collection centre was not within our jurisdiction, had to do with the report about the activities of the Green Berets in Kozarac where several civilians stated that they were used as a human shield and that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: -- Sulejman, aka Kole, who was one of the ring leaders, would not let them leave. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, sir, when you came back from Banja Luka to Prijedor, you would have gone through Kozarac, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so you do, in fact, know there was widespread destruction of civilian homes there, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You could see that when you passed by.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: You see, during combat the road between Prijedor and Banja Luka via Kozarac was not open for traffic. However, with a corps colonel, I travelled that route at own risk just one or two days after the combat. I could observe a number of houses that had been torched immediately next to the road. That's what I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which colonel were you travelling with?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I think it was Cendic. I think he was in the logistics base and worked on logistical support.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: It's difficult. Cendic. In any case, I think he was from Serbia proper because he spoke in the Ekavian dialect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P2895.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document signed by Simo Drljaca. Directing your attention to point 3, we read: "A mixed group consisting of national, public, and military security investigators shall be responsible for the work with and categorisation of detainees. They shall organise themselves respecting the parity principle. Mirko Jesic, Ranko Mijic, and Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic shall be responsible for their work." Now, Mirko Jesic was from the SNB national security right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Rajko Mijic, Prijedor SJB, public security?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic is your boss; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: As for the question whether he was my boss, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're aware that other interrogators from the security and intelligence organ of the 43rd Brigade under Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic took part in the work with and categorisation of detainees at Omarska; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic was in Omarska before he became the assistant commander. He was sent from the 1st Krajina Corps to the interrogation centre in Omarska. When he was appointed assistant commander in the 43rd Motorised Brigade as my boss, he no longer went to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We lost signal, it seems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have to see whether -- I see that the connection has been restored. Witness, halfway your answer, the connection was interrupted. I read what we still --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can repeat my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would resume from where you said "when he was appointed assistant commander in the 43rd Motorised Brigade as my boss, he no longer went to," and could you please resume from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to my knowledge, he no longer went to interrogate in Omarska. My knowledge is that at the time when he interrogated there, it pertains to the time when he was still with the Krajina Corps when he was still not a member of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You said that he was sent from the 1st Krajina Corps to Omarska. Do you also know who sent him?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask for 65 ter 32253. I apologise, this isn't in the witness's package. I'm going to direct him to one specific point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is a dispatch sent by Prijedor SJB Chief Drljaca to CSB Banja Luka on the 13th of June, 1992. And Mr. Lukic will correct me if I'm wrong, I'm sure. But it describes some events. And at the bottom, it says: "All operatives and the team of experts who worked under the supervision of Mirko Jesic and Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic can confirm that these allegations are true." So as of the 13th of June, Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic was still supervising operatives and a team of experts in Omarska; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, we only have the B/C/S version before us at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I see that, Your Honour. I'm not certain how that's happened, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The English translation is uploaded?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was there, I'm told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which paragraph are you reading, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm reading at the end. We still have the previous document's English on the screen. If we could ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Apparently we have an upload issue. I think I can put the proposition to the witness and ask that it be MFI'd, if that suits the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections by Mr. Lukic, who is able to read the original. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, what I was putting to you was that as the document on our screens reflects, as of the 13th of June, 1992, Lieutenant-Colonel Majstorovic was still supervising operatives and a team of experts at Omarska; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. But before the 30th of June, he was not the assistant commander for intelligence and security. It was Lieutenant Todic, as far as I remember. He only joined after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this document be marked for identification and we'll check the upload.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 32253 will receive number P7209.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification. Mr. Traldi, I'm looking at the clock. You are -- you said half an hour?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I have about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would -- Mr. Lukic, would a little bit over half an hour do for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It will be sufficient, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally, sir, on Keraterm, you refer in your statement to an incident the night of the 24 to 25th of July where 150 people were killed you said you heard about it. Now at the time, you and the 43rd Brigade command were both based across the street from Keraterm in the Kozara Putevi building; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And because you were based across the street from Keraterm, you must have known that crimes had been being committed against the people detained there throughout the summer of 1992: Beatings, sexual violence, killings. You knew that at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: From other people's stories, I personally never witnessed any such things, so I can't testify about them. I just heard stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You heard stories. Other people in the Kozara Putevi building, where the brigade command was based, would also have heard those stories; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when you heard that detained persons were being beaten or being raped or being killed, you didn't keep that information to yourself, did you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I believe that the security organ had more than we in the intelligence part of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you would tell your superior, right, when you heard a story like that?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I believe that I heard accurate information during the debriefings when somebody from the security organ informed us about that event, that the motive was retaliation, and that members of the 43rd Motorised Brigade were not involved. This is what I heard. This is the information I was privy to but I never checked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You never checked it. You were based across the street. You knew there were military police based in Keraterm. There was no investigation by you or your organ whatsoever, was there?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, in fact, you have no idea whether VRS soldiers were among the perpetrators because you didn't investigate; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: The first piece of official information was that the whole event was just revenge for the death of a dead policeman. That's all I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, that's about motive. It's not about perpetrators. You don't have any idea who the perpetrators were. You didn't in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Not then, not after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So what I'd put to you is, in fact, there was no investigation not because you knew the crime was outside the VRS's jurisdiction but because -- but for the same reason that Zigic and Dosen were released when they were arrested, that they were sent back to the front, because the policy was not to punish soldiers who committed crimes against Muslims and Croats even if the crime was mass murder; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: That was not the way I was thinking or acting, nor did I have information to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And because you were across the street, you knew that just before that crime, hundreds of prisoners had been brought into Keraterm as a result of cleansing operations in the Brdo and Biscani areas; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I knew that there were hundreds. I knew that they had been brought to Keraterm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You knew a room had been cleared out for them?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I don't know how the space was obtained, but I know that they were accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you know they were put in the same room together?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I was present during the year 1992 when the international commission came and inspected Keraterm. They paid attention to the first room which was closest to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: It was a somewhat larger room, but I never knew that they were all accommodated in that room.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you know as you sit here today that what we're talking about is room 3 where these people who had been picked up in Brdo and Biscani were put; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about the name of that room as being room number 3. I know that people were executed there from hearsay. I know that it was a case of retaliation. The figure that I heard was -- was over 150. I don't know how many; but, yes, it was a large figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The rest of the command also knew over 150 people had been killed; right?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your claim is 150 people are murdered across the street, and 23 years later you don't even know what room it happened in. That's your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time ever I hear it from you that it was room 3. I did not know that. Even yesterday I didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, any questions in re-examination for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do have questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I continue I forgot to tender, since it was MFI'd, D896.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist me in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the last document. The document that was issued by this gentleman, the list of Croats and Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'd like to look at it and compare it to the VOB if a full version is going to be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If Your Honours direct us to provide the whole VOB-8, we will do that. But we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the Prosecution thinks that it can better analyse the excerpt by having the full version of it. Under those circumstances, if you -- I think it's reasonable to disclose it, the complete version, to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have it yet, but I will ask Mr. Rodic, who is here with us, and tell him that we'll soon ask from him to provide us with the full version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, the Prosecution could do it itself as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to make clear all I was doing was, and perhaps inartfully, was inquiring whether that was going to happen. If not, then we could formulate a position now. But if it was, we would want to make the comparison.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you do not -- you're not asking for postponement of hearing your position? Because if Mr. Lukic wouldn't ask for it, that you would do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If there's no already an intention, then we wouldn't ask for a postponement of our position, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what then is your position if Mr. Lukic -- that you do not oppose admission?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We don't oppose admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll decide in due course on admission, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what about D768 and D769. Do you have any intentions?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes we want to tender them, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And the same should be true for D767?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We want to tender all four documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, all four. They have numbers already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would -- the Chamber will decide in due course on admission. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Can we have D767 in front of us so just the gentleman knows what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, Mr. Traldi, is your position in relation to the other documents the same; that is, no opposition and no ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes. The same. Regarding 767, I think we would want to reserve the right to request additional excerpts, but that's all we would do at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can always ask for additional excerpts which is, of course, not a condition for -- you'd say you can consider that even if it would be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. The Chamber will decide in due course on admission of these four documents. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we could have page 2 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rodic, let me ask you something about the list of conscripts, the so-called VOB-8. My learned friend Mr. Traldi mentioned that the last date in the book is the 30th of June, 1996. He also asked you whether it is possible that somebody's name was entered into the list on the 29th of February, 1996. Could you please tell us whether --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. We have Mr. Traldi on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. Just for the record, I think both months should have been March. And I'm not sure if there was an interpretation issue or a problem with the record earlier, but I'm fairly confident I referred to the 30th of March and the 29th as it was the day before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if that makes any difference for you, Mr. Lukic, are you willing to accept --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do accept this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please proceed as you deem appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, do you know if anybody's name was entered into the VOB-8 records on the 29th of March, 1996?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: I said no because we were not the author of a VOB-8 box. We are their custodians at the moment. But it is possible that the date is 16 September --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down. We need to be absolutely certain of the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, would you please slow down and could you repeat your answer. You said: "We are their custodians at the moment. But it is possible that the date is..." And could you then resume from there and be slow on especially the dates.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. What I'm saying that it is technically possible. The date is 16 September, 1991, and the other date is 30th March, 1996. So it is possible that somebody's name was entered on the 29th of March, 1996. I don't know whether it was done or not, whether any such cases exist. I don't know. I repeat, that I received the VOB-8 in 2005 in the month of February. I can only testify that this is authentic. I don't know how it was created.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on personnel files, would it be possible to see when an individual joined the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes. Personnel files for the officers, unit files for the other soldiers, they depict the exact dates, what their duration of service was during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We still believe that there are issues pending with this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call up P7203.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, you marked this photo. You marked the building that was used by the military police and where you also entered.

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What do you see when you are looking from that building in the direction of Keraterm? Can you see the inside of Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was it who provided security for the Muslims who were incarcerated in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: According to what I knew, it was MUP members who guarded them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you anything about their work? Did they report to you?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. For the first month or so, we were in constant conflict. I and Mr. Seric [phoen] from the intelligence service did not have access to Keraterm, although we needed intelligence about the Green Berets. We requested that information, but we were never accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you send some people to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: There was an incident. It was about half past 12.00 at night. Since there were no conditions for us to do our job in our small building, we wanted one of our interviewees to be accommodated in Keraterm that night, and we said that we would fetch him in the morning. When we came to fetch him the following morning, they wouldn't give him to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After that, did you continue sending people to Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No, no. When they were under our authority, we didn't -- we informed our superiors that the co-operation with the interrogators in Keraterm was not good, that a lot of intelligence is lost because it doesn't reach us or it is belated in reaching us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, let us look at P7205.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have seen this document. It is about the accused Zoran Zigic who was being released from custody because the presence of Zoran Zigic was guaranteed at a possible trial. We can see that in the third paragraph of the statement of reasons, and I'm going to ask you, sir: Do you know if Zoran Zigic killed somebody in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: No. There were rumours, but I wouldn't be able to give you any names. I heard that he did commit crimes, did -- they -- that he and Djole killed people, but I am not sure if that is true or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that he had killed a Serbian girl?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: There were stories about that, but I don't know any details. There were rumours to that effect. I heard that Djole had killed a lady called Jolenka, who was a secretary at the court, but I only heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. If you don't know any details, we'll move on. And now let me ask you about Trnopolje. Do you know how people ended up in Trnopolje? How did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: What I heard from our chief was that they used a corridor that was left open during fighting. Most of them arrived in that way. And then when the Red Cross, the Doctors Without Borders arrived, they arrived in the collection centre in Prijedor, and there were also those 50 that arrived from Keraterm and Manjaca. After the first large group left, the Muslims who resided in Prijedor in their own houses or who were staying with their relatives wanted to go to Trnopolje voluntarily because in there they saw their chance that a third country would receive them as immigrants. I remember a case when a man whose name I cannot remember told us a story about the money that he made in the course of one night. He made 4.000 convertible marks by transporting the people who wanted to join one of the convoys of an international organisations that organised those convoys for those who wanted to leave to a third country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What did you hear when people heard that they would be given an opportunity to go abroad, how many more people came to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: MISO RODIC
utterances.text: On the first day, a thousand more came. And then international organisations started restricting those numbers, and they made lists of those who were there already, and they said that they would no longer receive people in Trnopolje after that, that only those who were already on the lists were allowed to be there.
